Doh! Router maker D-Link accidentally publishes private cryptography keys

Why would I want router software silently installed on my computer in the first place? This is a much bigger security hole than just a simple leak, as it has existed before the leak. The leak made it public, but a Rouge employee could have exploited it too.

The key does not allow software to be installed on your computer, it verifies that the firmware being downloaded to the router is valid. If someone can own your router then they can probably own your computer, but one is not necessary for the other. Also, the cert has since expired, but it could call in to question any firmware you may have installed during that time it was active.

It was an incredibly stupid thing to have happened, and someone is probably going to be fired. But fsociety isn't coming for your porn stash with this key.
Isn't this good as it could make it easier to put 3rd party firmware on it like OpenWRT? It could install as easily as first-party updates.

You don't need a security cert to install OpenWRT, or any open source firmware. The cert only verified that the stock firmware updates being downloaded by the stock firmware really came from D-Link and not some third party. You can always just manually flash your own firmware, it's almost always as easy as downloading the correct file and then selecting it from a file section prompt in the stock firmware.
